::|scope resolution operator: Qualifies a name with the scope it belongs to: `std::cout` says "the `cout` inside namespace `std`", and a class uses it to define a member outside the class body (`Calculator::add`). See [Preprocessor & namespaces](#/comp3522/preprocessor-namespaces).
using|using namespace|namespace: A directive or declaration that pulls a name (or every name) out of a `namespace` — a named region that groups names so they don't collide with identically-named things elsewhere, e.g. the standard library's `std`. `using namespace std;` exposes everything in `std`; `using std::cout;` exposes only `cout`. See [Preprocessor & namespaces](#/comp3522/preprocessor-namespaces).
#include: A preprocessor directive that pastes the contents of a header file in place, before compilation starts — `#include <iostream>` pulls in the declarations for `cin`/`cout`. See [Preprocessor & namespaces](#/comp3522/preprocessor-namespaces).
#define: A preprocessor directive that does dumb text substitution before compilation: `#define PI 3.14159` replaces every later occurrence of `PI` with `3.14159`, with no type checking. `const`/`constexpr` are preferred for constants because they're type-checked. See [#define, const, constexpr](#/comp3522/constants).
#pragma once: A non-standard but universally supported preprocessor directive placed at the top of a header file so the compiler includes that header's contents only once per translation unit, even if it's `#include`d from multiple places. The portable alternative is an `#ifndef`/`#define`/`#endif` include guard. See [Header vs source files](#/comp3522/headers-sources).
#ifdef: A preprocessor conditional that includes the following code only if the named macro has been `#define`d; paired with `#endif`. Used (with `#ifndef`) to build include guards that stop a header being pasted twice. See [Header vs source files](#/comp3522/headers-sources).
declaration|header file|.hpp|.h: A `.h`/`.hpp` file holding **declarations** (function prototypes, class definitions) that other files `#include` so they know a name exists without needing its implementation yet — a declaration introduces a name/signature to the compiler without providing the full body. See [Header vs source files](#/comp3522/headers-sources).
definition|source file|.cpp: A `.cpp` file holding the actual **definitions** (function bodies) that get compiled into object code and then linked together. A name can be declared many times but defined only once (the one-definition rule). See [Header vs source files](#/comp3522/headers-sources).
bool: A 1-byte fundamental type holding `true` or `false`. Printed as `1`/`0` by `cout` unless `boolalpha` is set. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
char: A 1-byte fundamental type that stores a single character as its underlying integer code (e.g. `'A'` is `65`); `cout` prints it as a character, and casting it to `int` reveals the numeric code. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
short: An integer type that is at least 16 bits, usually smaller than `int`; used when memory matters more than range. `sizeof(short) <= sizeof(int) <= sizeof(long) <= sizeof(long long)`. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
int: The default integer type, typically 32 bits (range roughly ±2.1 billion, `numeric_limits<int>::max()` is `2147483647`). Use it for whole numbers unless you have a specific reason not to. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
long: An integer type at least as wide as `int` (commonly 32 or 64 bits depending on platform); `long long` is guaranteed at least 64 bits with max value `LLONG_MAX`. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
long long: A guaranteed-at-least-64-bit integer type, the widest standard integer; its maximum is `LLONG_MAX`. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
float: A single-precision floating-point type, roughly 6-7 significant decimal digits of precision, usually 4 bytes. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
double: A double-precision floating-point type, roughly 15-16 significant decimal digits, usually 8 bytes — the default choice for real numbers in C++. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
long double: An extended-precision floating-point type, at least as precise as `double` (precision is platform-dependent). See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
void: A type meaning "no value": a function returning `void` returns nothing, and `void` in a parameter list means the function takes no arguments. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
sizeof: An operator, evaluated at compile time, that returns the size in bytes of a type or expression, e.g. `sizeof(int)`. See [Ternary, comma, sizeof, bitwise](#/comp3522/assorted-ops).
numeric_limits|numeric_limits<int>::max(: A standard-library template, `std::numeric_limits<T>`, exposing compile-time facts about a type — `numeric_limits<int>::max()` gives the largest representable `int`. Requires `#include <limits>`. See [Types & variables](#/comp3522/types-variables).
const: A qualifier meaning a variable's value cannot change after initialization; the value can be known at compile time or only at run time (e.g. `const int constantinput = input;` from a runtime `input`). See [#define, const, constexpr](#/comp3522/constants).
constexpr: A qualifier meaning a variable's value must be computable at compile time; stronger than `const`, and required wherever the compiler needs a compile-time constant (like an array bound). See [#define, const, constexpr](#/comp3522/constants).
narrowing|-Wnarrowing: A conversion that can lose information, e.g. `int x{2.5};` truncating a `double` into an `int`. Brace initialization `{}` is the only form that catches this as a compiler error/warning (`-Wnarrowing`); `=` and `()` initialization allow it silently. See [Three ways to initialize](#/comp3522/initialization).
showpos: An I/O manipulator that forces a leading `+` on positive numbers, e.g. `cout << showpos << number;` prints `+123`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
hex: An I/O manipulator that switches integer output/input to base 16, e.g. `123` prints as `7b` (or `0x7b` with `showbase`). See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
oct: An I/O manipulator that switches integer output/input to base 8. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
dec: An I/O manipulator that switches integer output/input back to base 10 (the default). See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
uppercase: An I/O manipulator that makes hex digits and scientific-notation exponents print upper-case (`7B`, `E` instead of `e`). See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
showbase: An I/O manipulator that prints the base prefix for hex (`0x`) or octal (`0`) output, e.g. `showbase << hex` prints `0x7b` instead of `7b`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
left: An I/O manipulator that left-aligns the next field inside its `setw` width, padding on the right, e.g. `setw(6) << left` on `-123` prints `-123··`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
right: An I/O manipulator that right-aligns the next field inside its `setw` width, padding on the left (the default alignment). `setw(6) << right` on `-123` prints `··-123`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
internal: An I/O manipulator that pads between a number's sign and its digits, e.g. `setw(6) << internal` on `-123` prints `-··123`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
showpoint: An I/O manipulator that forces a decimal point (and trailing zeros to fill precision) even for whole-valued floats, e.g. `100.0` prints as `100.000` at precision 6 instead of `100`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
fixed: An I/O manipulator that prints floating-point numbers in fixed decimal notation (`123.4568` at precision 4) rather than scientific notation. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
scientific: An I/O manipulator that prints floating-point numbers in scientific notation, e.g. `123.456789` becomes `1.234568e+02`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
boolalpha: An I/O manipulator that prints/reads `bool` values as the words `true`/`false` instead of `1`/`0`; `noboolalpha` reverts to numeric. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
setw: An I/O manipulator taking a field width — `cout << setw(5) << number;` pads `number` to at least 5 characters for that one insertion only (it does not persist to the next `<<`). Needs `#include <iomanip>`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
setfill: An I/O manipulator that sets the padding character `setw` uses (default is a space), e.g. `setfill('*') << setw(5)` pads with `*`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
setprecision: An I/O manipulator setting how many digits are shown: total significant digits by default, or digits after the decimal point when combined with `fixed`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
setf: The `ios_base` member function form of setting a format flag, e.g. `cout.setf(ios_base::showpos);` or, with a second argument restricted to a field, `cout.setf(ios_base::hex, ios_base::basefield);`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
unsetf: The `ios_base` member function that clears a format flag previously set with `setf`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
ios_base|std::ios_base: The base class of the iostream hierarchy that holds formatting state: the flags (`fmtflags`), the fields they group into (`basefield`, `floatfield`, `adjustfield`), and the error-state bits (`iostate`). See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
fmtflags|ios_base::fmtflags: The bitmask type of every individual formatting flag (`hex`, `showpos`, `fixed`, ...), settable/clearable with `setf`/`unsetf`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
basefield|ios_base::basefield: The `fmtflags` group covering the integer base flags `hex`/`oct`/`dec`, so `setf(hex, basefield)` sets hex without disturbing unrelated flags. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
floatfield|ios_base::floatfield: The `fmtflags` group covering the float-notation flags `fixed`/`scientific`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
adjustfield|ios_base::adjustfield: The `fmtflags` group covering the alignment flags `left`/`right`/`internal`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
failbit: An `ios_base::iostate` bit set when a stream operation fails recoverably — most commonly `cin >>` reading text into a numeric variable. Once set, further extractions are skipped until `clear()`. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
badbit: An `ios_base::iostate` bit set on a serious, usually unrecoverable I/O error (like a broken stream buffer), distinct from the ordinary `failbit` mismatch. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
eofbit: An `ios_base::iostate` bit set once a read reaches end-of-input; typically checked via `while (cin >> n)`, which stops the loop cleanly on EOF. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
goodbit: The `ios_base::iostate` value meaning no error bits are set — the stream is fully usable. `cin.good()` returns true exactly when the state equals `goodbit`. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
fail(): A stream member function returning true if `failbit` or `badbit` is set — the general "did the last operation fail" check. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
bad(): A stream member function returning true only if `badbit` is set (a serious I/O error), narrower than `fail()`. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
eof(): A stream member function returning true if `eofbit` is set — end of input has been reached. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
good(): A stream member function returning true only when no error bits at all are set (state is `goodbit`). See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
clear(): A stream member function that resets the error state back to `goodbit` so the stream can be used again after a failed extraction; it does not remove the bad characters sitting in the buffer — pair it with `ignore()`. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
ignore()|cin.ignore(...): A stream member function that discards up to N characters from the input buffer (or until a delimiter), used after `clear()` to flush the leftover bad input that caused a failure — e.g. `cin.ignore(numeric_limits<streamsize>::max(), '\n')` discards the rest of the current line. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
streamsize|numeric_limits<streamsize>::m: The signed integer type streams use for sizes and counts, e.g. the argument type of `ignore()`. `numeric_limits<streamsize>::max()` means "as many as it takes". See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
LLONG_MAX: A macro (from `<climits>`) giving the largest value representable by `long long`; `numeric_limits<long long>::max()` is the type-safe C++ equivalent. See [When input fails](#/comp3522/input-failure).
?:|ternary operator: The only ternary operator in C++: `condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse` evaluates to one of the two branches depending on `condition`, without needing an `if`/`else` statement. See [Ternary, comma, sizeof, bitwise](#/comp3522/assorted-ops).
comma operator|,: The `,` operator evaluates its left operand, discards the result, then evaluates and returns its right operand — `int m = (a, b);` assigns `b`'s value to `m`. Rare outside `for`-loop headers; not the same as separating function arguments. See [Ternary, comma, sizeof, bitwise](#/comp3522/assorted-ops).
short-circuit|short-circuit evaluation|&: The rule that `&&` and `||` stop evaluating as soon as the result is determined: `false && x()` never calls `x()`, and `true || y()` never calls `y()`. See [++/--, relational & logical](#/comp3522/increment-logic).
++|increment operator: The increment operator. Prefix `++x` increments then evaluates to the new value; postfix `x++` evaluates to the old value, then increments. See [++/--, relational & logical](#/comp3522/increment-logic).
--|decrement operator: The decrement operator, with the same prefix/postfix distinction as `++`: `--x` decrements then returns the new value, `x--` returns the old value then decrements. See [++/--, relational & logical](#/comp3522/increment-logic).
%|modulo operator: The integer remainder operator: `17 % 5` is `2` (since `17 = 3*5 + 2`), and it satisfies `(a/b)*b + a%b == a`. Undefined behaviour if the right operand is `0`. See [Arithmetic & compound operators](#/comp3522/arithmetic).
/|division operator: The division operator: integer `/` integer truncates toward zero (`7/2` is `3`, `-7/2` is `-3`); if either operand is floating-point the result is a real division. Dividing an integer by `0` is undefined behaviour; dividing a floating-point value by `0.0` yields `inf`. See [Arithmetic & compound operators](#/comp3522/arithmetic).
C-style cast|(int)|static_cast: A cast written as `(Type)expression` (e.g. `(int)2.75` truncates to `2`) that forces a type conversion. Modern C++ prefers the named casts — `static_cast`, `dynamic_cast`, `const_cast`, `reinterpret_cast` — because they document intent and are individually greppable. See [C-style casting](#/comp3522/casting).
CMake|CMakeLists.txt: A build-system generator: a `CMakeLists.txt` file describes targets and dependencies, and CMake produces the actual build files (Makefiles, etc.) that compile and link a multi-file C++ project. See [Header vs source files](#/comp3522/headers-sources).
-Wall: A g++/clang flag enabling most useful warnings (unused variables, suspicious comparisons, etc.); commonly combined with `-Wextra -pedantic` for stricter checking. See [Anatomy of Hello World](#/comp3522/hello-world).
cout|std::cout: The standard output stream object (`std::cout`), used with `<<` to print to the console: `cout << "Hello world!" << endl;`. See [Anatomy of Hello World](#/comp3522/hello-world).
<<|stream insertion operator: The stream insertion operator, overloaded by `ostream` to mean "send this value to the stream": `cout << a << b;` inserts `a` then `b` in sequence. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
>>|stream extraction operator: The stream extraction operator, overloaded by `istream` to mean "pull a value out of the stream into this variable": `cin >> m >> n;` reads two whitespace-separated values in order. See [Reading input with cin](#/comp3522/input-cin).
endl|std::endl: A manipulator that inserts a newline character and flushes the output buffer, e.g. `cout << "n = " << n << endl;`. `'\n'` is the cheaper equivalent when a flush isn't needed. See [Anatomy of Hello World](#/comp3522/hello-world).
ostream: The output stream class (base of `cout`, file/string output streams); overloads `<<` for the built-in types and can be extended with a custom `operator<<`. See [Formatting output](#/comp3522/output-formatting).
istream|cin|std::cin: The input stream class (base of `cin`, file/string input streams); overloads `>>` for the built-in types, skipping leading whitespace by default. `std::cin` is the standard input stream object, used with `>>` to read from the console, e.g. `cin >> n;`. See [Reading input with cin](#/comp3522/input-cin).
